title: Getting ready to sell in Tasmania
description: What to gather before you list a Tasmanian home. Tasmania has no compulsory vendor statement, so buyers rely on the contract, council records and inspections. Summarised from Consumer Affairs Tasmania and council guidance.

sources.title: Advice when buying or selling property

items.title: Engage a licensed conveyancer or lawyer
Have them prepare the Tasmanian standard contract for the sale of real estate, and decide on optional clauses such as vendor disclosure and cooling-off
Give them your title details and any easements or covenants you know of
Order a 337 certificate (land information certificate) from your council
items.detail: Shows completion certificates, occupancy permits and enforcement action.

items.title: Gather building and plumbing permits and certificates of completion for work on the property
Ask a building surveyor about any work without approvals
items.detail: A certificate of substantial compliance may be possible.

items.title: Ask your lender for the discharge form and payout figure
Give your conveyancer the body corporate manager's contact
Test the smoke alarms and replace any replaceable-battery alarms
Check the pool barrier and gate self-close and latch
If tenanted, check the lease end date and notice rules
Have your power of attorney, probate or other authority to sell ready
